heard: The most famous cow in history never kicked that lantern. On October 8, 1871, a devastating fire broke out onto Coven Street. Fueled by severe drought, the Great Chicago Fire killed about 300 people. Seeking a scapegoat, journalist Michael Ahearn blamed Irish immigrant Catherine O'Leary. He claimed her cow kicked a lantern, but O'Leary was asleep in bed. Ahearn later admitted he fabricated the entire story for a colorful headline. Chicago took 126 years to officially clear her name.
differences: 'on dekoven' heard as 'onto coven' after 'fire broke out'
